advisor_identified: Glenn O. Phillips, historian of the Caribbean and African diaspora, professor of history at Morgan State University.

doctorate.title: The Changing Role of the Merchant Class in the British West Indies, 1834-1867

evidence.says: The 2010-2013 graduate catalogue, printed p. 344 (PDF p. 354), lists Glenn O. Phillips as professor of history and gives his PhD institution as Howard University.
The Maritime History Research Collection lists Phillips, Glenn O.I., The Changing Role of the Merchant Class in the British West Indies, 1834-1867, as a PhD thesis at Howard University, 1976.
Glenn O. Phillips, identified with Morgan State University, lists the same dissertation under Glenn Phillips among Howard history dissertations and dates it 1976 (PDF p. 13).

Dibua’s institutional CV, p. 15, records Godfrey Vincent’s 2011 Morgan State history dissertation on empowering workers through the Oilfields Workers’ Trade Union, 1962-1987, with Dibua as first reader.

notes: Institution, year and title match the linked record. The student entry lacks a university; its topic and date appear to correspond to Godfrey Vincent’s dissertation under a revised title. Phillips’s supervision of that student was not independently confirmed, but his contemporary Morgan State appointment and Howard doctorate are corroborated.
